Chief_Complaint.source_text: CC: Difficulty breathing after insect sting

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Patient was stung on the arm minutes ago.
Arm is rashy and red with a puncture mark at the sting site.
Patient feels slightly anxious after the sting.
Patient reports possible mild right-sided lip swelling.
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: reports possible mild R-sided lip swelling

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Patient reports tongue feels a bit weird.
Patient does not feel breathing difficulty is particularly acute.
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: Currently: Does not feel breathing difficulty is particularly acute

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Patient sought advice in case symptoms worsen.
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: sought advice in case it worsens

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Patient has not taken any antihistamines yet.
Patient has never had an EpiPen.
Patient denies allergies to pets or food.

Past_Medical_History.content: History of episodic anxiety/panic, no medications.

Adverse_Drug_Reactions_and_Allergies.content: Denies allergies to pets or food.

Family_History.content: Patient denies family history of acute reactions or illnesses.

Social_and_Family_History.content: Patient works as a computer scientist.

Assessment.content: Localized reaction to insect sting (bee/wasp) — mild; no clinical features of anaphylaxis.
Assessment.source_text: 1) Localized reaction to insect sting (bee/wasp) — mild; no clinical features of anaphylaxis

Plan_of_Care.content: Recommend over-the-counter antihistamine chlorphenamine (Piriton) 4 mg tablet, up to approximately 6 times per day, or a once-daily non-sedating antihistamine as preferred.
Plan_of_Care.source_text: OTC antihistamine: Chlorphenamine (Piriton) 4 mg tablet, up to ~6x/day; or a once-daily non-sedating antihistamine as preferred

Plan_of_Care.content: Safety net advice to seek urgent care/A&E if lip or tongue swelling, shortness of breath, stridor, or rapid progression occurs.
Plan_of_Care.source_text: Safety-net: Seek urgent care/A&E if lip/tongue swelling, SOB, stridor, or rapid progression

Plan_of_Care.content: Monitor sting site and consider antibiotics if redness spreads, feels hot, or signs of local infection develop.
Plan_of_Care.source_text: Monitor sting site; if redness spreads/feels hot or signs of local infection, consider abx

Plan_of_Care.content: Provided information link on anaphylaxis and advised low threshold to contact clinic.
Plan_of_Care.source_text: Provided info link on anaphylaxis; advised low threshold to contact clinic

Plan_of_Care.content: Reassurance given for anxiety and advised to reach out if worries persist or symptoms change.
Plan_of_Care.source_text: Reassurance; advised to reach out if worries persist or symptoms change

Follow_up_Information.content: Advised low threshold to contact clinic if concerned.
Follow_up_Information.source_text: advised low threshold to contact clinic

Follow_up_Information.content: Advised to reach out if worries persist or symptoms change.
Follow_up_Information.source_text: advised to reach out if worries persist or symptoms change

Physical_Findings.content: On video exam, patient is speaking comfortably and breathing seems all right to examiner with no stridor observed.
Physical_Findings.source_text: Gen/Resp (via video): Speaking comfortably; breathing “seems all right” to examiner; no stridor observed

Physical_Findings.content: Lips are not visibly swollen to examiner.
Physical_Findings.source_text: Lips: Not visibly swollen to examiner

Physical_Findings.content: Oropharyngeal exam via video shows adequate view with no concerning swelling seen.
Physical_Findings.source_text: OP exam (video): Adequate view; no concerning swelling seen

Physical_Findings.content: Skin of arm shows slight erythema with puncture mark and blotchy rash with no obvious swelling.
Physical_Findings.source_text: Skin (arm): Slight erythema with puncture mark; blotchy rash; no obvious swelling
